record.abstract: In vehicular integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) networks, each service-provider vehicle uses a limited power budget to serve multiple sensing targets and communication receivers. Maximizing the communication sum-rate subject to sensing signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) constraints is nonconvex, and iterative optimization is costly to rerun for every network layout. This paper proposes a graph neural network (GNN)-based power allocation algorithm, termed GNN-ISAC. Concretely, GNN-ISAC addresses the aforementioned problem by considering two distinct edge types in the graph representation, one capturing the inter-provider interference, the other representing the intra-provider power-budget sharing. GNN-ISAC is trained without labels using a sensing-penalized sum-rate loss. We also adapt the weighted mean-square error minimization (WMMSE) algorithm to this problem by introducing a sensing-power reservation step. Simulation results show that GNN-ISAC achieves communication sum-rates close to WMMSE with low sensing-link violation rates and much less computation. It also outperforms an existing heterogeneous GNN and a channel-blind baseline, and generalizes to larger networks without retraining.

record.abstract: Implicit neural representations (INRs) model signals as continuous functions from coordinates to values, but their performance depends strongly on how spectral capacity is allocated. Yet most Quantum INR (QINR) architectures treat spectral components as independent outputs of separate quantum blocks. We introduce the Spectral Quantum Memory Model (SQMM), a memory coupled quantum INR in which sequential hybrid data reuploading layers (bands) communicate through a shared coherent quantum memory register. Each band reads the memory, computes on its own coordinate upload, and writes part of its state back, so later bands can build on the computation of earlier ones. When memory read and write layers are input independent, we prove that the memory state forms an operator valued Fourier series whose support is contained in the Minkowski sum of the initial memory spectrum and the local band spectra. Downstream bands then condition their Fourier coefficients on the spectral content stored by earlier bands, and the memory coupling creates no new primitive frequencies. This theory motivates a spectral memory alignment loss that encourages memory to encode the spectrum expressed by the deployed prefix of the model. Across audio and image reconstruction benchmarks, SQMM improves over compact QINR and INR baselines.

record.abstract: A double-transmon coupler (DTC) enables a fast, high-fidelity CZ gate between two highly detuned, fixed-frequency transmon qubits. Moreover, a recently proposed capacitively shunted DTC (CSDTC) realizes a small residual ZZ interaction over a wide flux-bias range around zero flux, eliminating the necessity of static flux biasing while maintaining high CZ-gate fidelity. However, CZ gates with the DTC and CSDTC require baseband flux pulses with large amplitudes, which are vulnerable to pulse distortion and decoherence due to large qubit-coupler hybridization. To address these issues, we experimentally demonstrate a parametrically driven iSWAP gate operated at zero flux bias between highly detuned, fixed-frequency transmon qubits coupled through a CSDTC. Using a simple flux-drive waveform without predistortion, we realize an average gate fidelity of 99.92(2)% at a total gate time of 112 ns. The observed high-fidelity performance is consistent with small qubit-coupler hybridization and small effective ZZ interaction during the gate. Our numerical simulations reproduce the experimentally observed iSWAP interaction rate and effective ZZ interaction, demonstrating the applicability of the theoretical model not only to spectral information but also to time-domain dynamics such as gate operations. These results boost further progress in the research of superconducting quantum computers.

record.abstract: Object detection research remains constrained by high annotation costs and the closed-set assumptions of supervised models, limiting scalability to novel categories. We present a target-dataset annotation-free object detection framework that eliminates the need for human labeling on the target dataset by leveraging the complementary strengths of pretrained foundation models, including segmentation and vision-language systems, combined with a self-refining training loop. To further reduce reliance on expensive LVLM queries, we introduce a landmark-based clustering mechanism that amortizes labeling across image clusters, improving label consistency while lowering computational cost. Our method autonomously generates segmentation proposals, assigns semantic labels through multimodal reasoning, and iteratively improves both localization and classification using a lightweight open-set detector. This modular pipeline enables adaptation to completely unseen object classes and domains without any human-provided target-dataset annotations, while maintaining compatibility with existing detection architectures. Evaluations on COCO, LVIS, ODinW-35, and Roboflow-100 demonstrate substantial performance gains over state-of-the-art open-vocabulary and long-tail detection methods, achieving 60.8 AP on COCO and 47.4 AP on LVIS under zero-shot settings. Beyond strong benchmark results, our approach provides a scalable foundation for real-world detection systems in unknown environments, where annotation is infeasible.

record.abstract: Deep learning models for brain tumor MRI classification are usually compared by accuracy alone, on public datasets whose independence is rarely checked. We benchmarked six architectures: two convolutional networks (EfficientNetV2-M and ConvNeXt-V2-Tiny), two vision transformers (Swin-V2-S and ViT-L/16), and two foundation models (DINOv2-L and MedSigLIP-448), for four-class classification of 7,216 public MRI images. We assessed accuracy, calibration, explainability, ensembles, and decision curves, with every fitted quantity estimated on validation data only. Pixel-verified duplicate screening showed that 36% of the test images had a near-duplicate in the training data. Test accuracy ranged from 94.5% to 95.6%, with no pairwise difference after Holm correction, and fell to 90.3% to 91.7% on the 773 test images free of duplicates and shared patients. Ensembles did not outperform the best single model. Attribution maps passed a model-randomization test but localized expert-annotated tumors poorly. On 1,675 external BDNeuro-MRI images that did not duplicate the training data, accuracy ranged from 77.6% (MedSigLIP-448) to 95.0% (ViT-L/16), and 12 of 15 pairwise differences were significant. Internal accuracy on this public collection therefore did not distinguish the architectures, whereas the duplicate-filtered external test did.

record.abstract: Digital Twins are evolving from passive virtual representations into closed-loop systems that continuously synchronize with physical assets and drive real-time decisions. Yet predictive modeling, machine learning (ML), uncertainty quantification (UQ), and decision-making have been studied as separate capabilities, leaving limited understanding of their integration and maintenance during online operation. This narrative review, scoped by the functional requirements of real-time decision-making rather than by Digital Twin terminology alone, examines how such decisions are generated and sustained in engineering Digital Twins. We first examine foundational decision-making architectures and representative engineering applications, followed by methods that address their limitations across the decision loop. We identify optimization-based, policy-based, and knowledge-based approaches as the major pathways from virtual representation to action. Across them, ML plays three roles in decision-making: enabling efficient surrogate modeling, transforming heterogeneous physical feedback into decision-relevant information, and accelerating or directly generating decisions. UQ supports uncertainty-aware decisions and model adaptation, while continual validation, drift detection, and adaptation help maintain reliable operation as the physical system evolves. Together, these findings underscore the need for a shift from a model-centric to a system-centric perspective on Digital Twins, where its performance depends on the interactions with sensing, state estimation, computation, decision-making, and adaptation rather than on their standalone performance. Therefore, future research should shift from isolated algorithm development toward system-level co-design, scalable decision-making, and approaches to design, and data-efficient continual adaptation and validation for AI-enabled autonomous systems.

record.abstract: This paper presents a distributed model predictive control (MPC) architecture for collision-avoiding motion planning of planar robots with double-integrator dynamics. To reduce coordination demands, a time-varying predicted conflict graph selects relevant pairwise interactions. The associated collision-avoidance constraints are convexified once per MPC update using warm-start trajectories, yielding a fixed convex quadratic program (QP). The resulting QP is then decomposed using an edge-consensus formulation of the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM), enabling parallel robot-local optimization and independent closed-form projections onto separating half-spaces. Execution is selectively supervised by a centralized high-order control barrier function (HOCBF) QP when the distributed candidate does not satisfy the direct-execution conditions. Evaluated in C++ simulations involving 8, 16, and 32 robots, the proposed architecture achieves collision-free execution and substantially improves computational scalability while maintaining task-level performance comparable to a centralized complete-graph baseline.

record.abstract: Financial fraud screening operates under fixed investigation capacity, so overall discrimination may not indicate how many fraudulent transactions reach reviewers. The no-rule-bonus variant still gates anomaly evidence and reaches 14.96%; a truly ungated supervised-anomaly baseline reaches 14.05%. This separates anomaly gating from direct rule-score uplift. Budget and review-window analyses show that the marginal value of explicit rule gating depends on the allocation policy and validation-selected coefficients. The central contribution is a reproducible test of when an auditable hybrid changes a restricted review queue, including cases where added components provide no benefit. record.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) requires large amounts of interaction data or a reliable simulator, both hard to obtain for nonlinear soft robotic hardware. Recent work shows that a time-scale separation inherent to soft robot dynamics justifies their reduction to low-dimensional invariant manifolds, known as adiabatic spectral submanifolds (aSSMs). We demonstrate that an aSSM-reduced model, a simple polynomial ordinary differential equation learned purely from pre-collected data, can serve as an RL training environment. On a pneumatically actuated soft arm, we train a trajectory-tracking policy in 3 hours on a six-dimensional aSSM-reduced model and deploy it without fine-tuning, whereas reproducing this policy training extrapolates to 3 years of hardware interaction. record.abstract: Abstract We analyze black hole (BH) scaling relations at the high-mass end, focusing in particular on the regime of ultramassive black holes, M BH > 10 10 M ⊙ (UMBHs). This first sample of triaxial BH mass determinations increases the number of known UMBHs by a factor of 2 and dramatically increases the constraints for BH mass scaling relations at the high-mass end. We find that BCGs are outliers in the canonical M BH ∝ σ 4−5 relation, while the size of their depleted cores—the central light-deficient region—offers a tighter correlation with M BH with a scatter of 0.22 dex in this mass regime, confirming and extending earlier findings that core size provides a robust proxy at the high-mass end. Our measurements smoothly join the trend already established in previous studies. This also holds for tight correlations between core size and sphere-of-influence radius and core size and core density, which, along with the correlation between M BH and core size, strongly support the BH binary model for the formation of the centers of the most massive galaxies, as the observed core sizes are inconsistent with gravitational-wave recoil predictions and the galaxies display central tangential orbital anisotropy expected from scouring.

record.abstract: Observation of the quantum Mpemba effect has spurred much interest in its enabling conditions and its relation to the classical counterpart. Here, we consider weakly open many-body quantum systems initialized in different thermal states and examine when the initially farther state relaxes to the (non-equilibrium) steady state faster. We claim that the number of conserved quantities in the unitary part plays a crucial role: the Mpemba effect is possible only when the Hamiltonian commutes with other extensive operators or is integrable. The reason lies in the dynamical evolution happening in spaces of different dimensions. When energy is the only approximately conserved quantity, dissipation pushes the dynamics within a single-parameter manifold of different thermal states. In contrast, for Hamiltonians with several conserved quantities, the dynamics drift in the multi-dimensional space of generalized Gibbs ensembles, whose distance to the steady state is less trivial. We provide numerical results for large system sizes using tensor networks and free-fermion techniques, thereby supporting our claim.

record.abstract: The tumour suppressor p53, encoded by TP53, is among the most frequently altered genes in human cancer yet it remains a challenging therapeutic target. Its role as a transcription factor, the absence of a conventional catalytic pocket and the diversity of oncogenic mutations have complicated the development of p53 directed small molecules. record.abstract: To track state of health (SOH), second-life potential and design warranties, it is necessary to accurately characterise lithium-ion battery capacity degradation. This paper compares the methodological approaches used for regression models of capacity fade, using synthetic degradation curves which are built from the structure of the publicly available Oxford Battery Degradation Dataset 1 (OBDD1) of eight 740 mAh cells discharged using an ARTEMIS urban drive-cycle at 40 °C, with each degradation profile sampled every 100 cycles. The quantitative results provided are thus illustrative, whereas the qualitative conclusions made on the problem of model selection are robust and extend to the real data. From the early-life extrapolation experiment, it can be observed that the remaining useful life is consistently overestimated by low-order polynomials and thus the motivation of using uncertainty-aware approaches. record.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-supported telemedicine may extend clinical expertise to rural communities, yet its benefits can be offset by unequal connectivity, digital literacy, data representation, and institutional readiness. This study examined the efficacy and health-equity implications of AI-powered telemedicine in post-pandemic rural Indonesia. A qualitative-dominant, convergent mixed-methods secondary study integrated reflexive thematic analysis of peer-reviewed qualitative evidence and Indonesian policy documents with descriptive synthesis of verified national and clinical datasets. Evidence included 2023 national internet statistics, a 63,012-person chronic-disease survey, a 311-patient rheumatology survey, and a 15-interview qualitative study. Telemedicine was most effective for stable follow-up, medication management, specialist access, and travel-cost avoidance, but was less reliable for first diagnosis, unstable disease, and examination-dependent care. Rural internet use (59.33%) remained 17.47 percentage points below urban use (76.80%). Among people with hypertension and/or diabetes, 98.0% reported no telemedicine use, indicating a substantial implementation gap. Four integrated themes emerged: conditional clinical efficacy, redistributed rather than eliminated access burdens, algorithmic amplification of structural disadvantage, and the necessity of human-mediated hybrid care. Conclusion: AI-powered telemedicine is neither inherently equalizing nor intrinsically exclusionary. record.abstract: Looped transformers apply a shared block several times per token to improve accuracy without adding parameters. The planner minimizes reads under budgets for predicted damage and storage. During decoding, each loop reads the high 2 bits of each 4-bit value and fetches the low bits only where its own attention weights require 4-bit precision. record.abstract: Generative world modeling from large-scale visual data offers a promising path toward scalable robot manipulation. We then train a world model that takes an image and a task description as input and predicts dense full-object flow over the reconstructed object geometry. record.abstract: Gravitational-wave data is never analysed without some conditioning: filtering and tapering act multiplicatively on the noise, destroying the stationarity on which the Whittle likelihood --- the backbone of nearly all gravitational-wave inference --- rests. The problem is particularly evident for LISA, where gaps are expected to overlap almost all signals and the noise must be estimated jointly with those astrophysical signals. We provide an analytical and numerical framework to assess the impact of noise mis-modelling when signal and noise parameters are inferred jointly in the presence of gaps. From a Fisher-matrix formalism verified against Bayesian inference, we obtain closed forms for the model uncertainties, their maximum-likelihood estimates and the true scatter in the latter, for various approximations to the likelihood. The Fisher-based linear formalism is extended through the Godambe--White curvature to the non-linear regime that severe mis-modelling produces. We survey gap families from long, well-tapered interruptions to short, high-rate ones, injecting massive black-hole binaries. Except in the case of frequent gaps, we show that the windowed covariance is well approximated by its leading diagonal --- the window convolved with the power spectral density --- for the estimation of both signal and noise parameters. By omitting the convolution, the signal sector remains unbiased but the noise parameters, in particular the optical-metrology noise which is dominant at high frequency, is displaced by over an order of magnitude in power. At the highest glitch rates the diagonal approximation stays accurate yet loses an order of magnitude in precision. To remedy this, we propose an exact time-domain likelihood of the surviving samples which can be efficiently (and accurately solved) via preconditioned conjugate gradient methods.

record.abstract: Hidden Markov models (HMMs) are powerful tools for analysing time series data that depend on discrete underlying but unobserved states. As such, they have gained prominence across numerous empirical disciplines, in particular ecology, medicine, and economics. However, the increasing complexity of empirical data is often accompanied by additional latent structure such as spatial effects, temporal trends, or measurement perturbations. Gaussian fields provide an attractive building block for incorporating such structured latent variation into HMMs. Fast inference methods for Gaussian fields have emerged through the stochastic partial differential equation (SPDE) approach. Due to their sparse representation, these integrate well with novel frequentist estimation methods for random-effects models via the use of automatic differentiation and the Laplace approximation. Scaling to high dimensions requires tools such as (R)TMB to exploit sparsity in the Hessian w.r.t. the latent variables - a property satisfied by SPDE fields but violated by the HMM likelihood. We present a modified forward algorithm to compute the HMM likelihood, constructing sparsity in the Hessian and consequently enabling fast and scalable inference. We demonstrate the practical feasibility and the usefulness through simulations and two case studies exploring the detection of stellar flares as well as modelling the movement of lions.

record.abstract: We study extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) evolving in a scalar cloud environment that may form through superradiant instabilities, using a fully relativistic perturbative framework that allows for eccentric and inclined orbits. EMRIs, consisting of a stellar-mass compact object inspiraling into a supermassive black hole, are key sources for space-based gravitational-wave detectors such as LISA. Previous relativistic studies of EMRIs in scalar clouds have been restricted to circular, equatorial motion. Here, instead, we focus on a Schwarzschild black hole background to incorporate eccentricity and orbital inclination. By computing the scalar energy and angular momentum scattered off to spatial infinity and absorbed at the event horizon, we show that orbital eccentricity can induce a dense spectrum of resonances near the last stable orbit, associated with strong relativistic apsidal precession. We further find that orbital inclination can significantly modify the orbital energy and angular momentum losses. In particular, we identify a critical inclination angle below which, at sufficiently small orbital radii, there is a net transfer of energy from the scalar cloud to the orbit. Moreover, for sufficiently large eccentricities, resonances associated with relativistic apsidal precession persist across the full range of inclinations, although their structure changes significantly between prograde and retrograde orbits. These results provide a foundation for future studies of EMRIs in scalar cloud environments on fully generic orbits around spinning black holes.

record.abstract: The integration of advanced materials and intelligent technologies is transforming sustainable engineering by enabling resource-efficient manufacturing, adaptive systems, real-time monitoring, and improved human–machine interaction. Conventional engineering approaches often rely on resource-intensive materials, energy-consuming processes, and limited monitoring capabilities, creating environmental and operational challenges throughout product life cycles. Advanced materials, including conductive polymers, nanofibers, stimuli-responsive polymers, shape-memory materials, photovoltaic fibers, and flexible electronic structures, offer opportunities to address these challenges through multifunctionality, lightweight design, and improved system adaptability. Concurrently, intelligent technologies, such as embedded sensors, digital monitoring systems, data-driven decision support, and connected wearable devices, support more efficient resource utilization and condition-based operation. Smart textiles provide a particularly relevant example because they combine material innovation with sensing, communication, energy harvesting, and user-oriented functionality. Applications in healthcare, industrial safety, energy management, environmental monitoring, and engineering education demonstrate the interdisciplinary potential of these technologies. However, their sustainable implementation requires careful consideration of material toxicity, manufacturing energy, durability, washability, electronic waste, recyclability, data privacy, and economic accessibility. This paper presents a literature-based technical review of advanced materials and intelligent technologies for sustainable engineering applications. It examines material characteristics, technological integration, application domains, environmental considerations, and implementation barriers. It also discusses life-cycle assessment, circular product design, sustainability-oriented engineering education, and challenge-based learning as complementary strategies for responsible innovation. The review indicates that technological performance alone is insufficient to establish sustainability; environmental integrity, human well-being, economic feasibility, and end-of-life management must be considered together. An integrated framework combining sustainable material selection, intelligent system design, lifecycle evaluation, and interdisciplinary education is proposed to guide future research and engineering practice.

record.abstract: Ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) requires the calculation of highly accurate electronic-structure energies and nuclear forces at every time step, which can quickly become computationally expensive. With SqDRIFT-AIMD, we obtain more accurate ground-state energies than the conventional coupled-cluster singles and doubles (CCSD) driven AIMD simulation for the $40$-qubit active space. We apply SqDRIFT-AIMD to study the dynamics of proton transfer in the Zundel cation, using circuits executed on IBM Heron r3 quantum processors. SqDRIFT energies fall below CCSD across the $40$-qubit double-well PES and stay within a few m$E_\text{h}$ of CCSD at 52 qubits. The $40$-qubit SqDRIFT-AIMD trajectory tracks the SHCI-driven proton transfer to within $1.33$ mÅ and exhibits excellent total energy conservation, with a standard deviation of only $0.245$ m$E_\text{h}$. record.abstract: In Constitutional AI, a plain-text "constitution" encodes values and gets incorporated into a model via post-training. However, the procedure for creating such a constitution poses significant challenges: who contributes, who decides which norms are included, and to what extent must the process be participatory or democratic? These challenges can be paralyzing. Yet, we argue that taking action is essential: without a deliberate constitution, sovereign models would risk misalignment or default to norms set by frontier model providers. We propose treating the development of a constitution as an evolving, participatory process akin to citizen science, iteratively drafted, tested, and refined. We therefore formulate five desirable principles: iterative, modular, justifiable, positional, and legitimate. We further argue that such a document must remain responsive not only over time but across the people it governs, and propose that provisions be marked as settled, contested, or underdetermined, so that durable disagreement is recorded in the constitution rather than resolved away. Empirically, we show via agent-based modelling that proposed process for maintaining living constitutions is robust against 50% bad actors among citizens - assuming a share of 75% participants with good intent in the deliberative body. This indicates that the proposed process tolerates a substantial share of adversarial participants.

record.abstract: We show that proximity to a $d_{xy}$-wave altermagnet provides an effective route to engineering boundary-geometry-dependent higher-order topological phases. The boundary geometry plays a crucial role in determining the topological properties: axis-aligned edge states remain gapless, whereas diagonal edges acquire effective masses with alternating signs, giving rise to four corner modes localized at the mass domain walls. By projecting onto the edge-state subspace, we derive the effective edge Hamiltonians for different boundary geometries. Furthermore, $π$-flux defects introduced under periodic boundary conditions yield zero-energy bound states localized at the flux cores, providing complementary evidence for nontrivial topology without physical boundaries. The interplay between the Zeeman field and the altermagnetic order drives a topological transition through the closing and reopening of the edge gap, while the bulk gap remains open. These findings highlight the crucial role of boundary geometry in higher-order topology and establish proximity-induced $d_{xy}$-wave altermagnetism as a route to engineering higher-order topological phases.

record.abstract: Underwater acoustic communication faces challenges such as limited available bandwidth and complex channel environments, which impose demanding requirements on efficient image transmission and reliable reconstruction. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a generative image communication framework based on cross-modal semantic successive refinement. At the transmitter, text descriptions, compact bottleneck features, and visual side information compressed by residual vector quantization are transmitted. At the receiver, text and bottleneck features are first fused to predict a base estimate of the intermediate visual representation. The received RVQ indices are then used to recover supplementary visual information and perform residual correction, followed by image reconstruction using a one-step Pixel Mean Flow model. During training, a CLIP-based text-image semantic consistency constraint is introduced to preserve the semantic correspondence between generated results and the original text descriptions. During transmission, protection resources are allocated according to the importance of different information branches and RVQ quantization stages. Simulations using COCO 2017 images and measured underwater acoustic channel records from Watermark show that text and bottleneck features provide complementary semantic and structural conditions, RVQ visual side information further improves reconstruction quality, and layered unequal error protection helps improve recovery at low SNRs. record.abstract: Parallel drafters accelerate LLM decoding by proposing a whole block of draft tokens in a single forward pass, making them attractive for LLM serving. Recent systems optimize goodput (i.e., accepted tokens per second) because rejected drafts steal compute from other requests. However, these systems control only how many tokens are verified, so every request still drafts a full block. At high serving load, we find that drafting consumes up to 40% of step time, of which a majority is discarded because it is never verified. Yet, draft-length control from autoregressive drafters does not carry over, because a parallel drafter commits to its length before its single pass. Moreover, draft and verification lengths are coupled across the batch, so they must be selected jointly for every request while keeping the decision computationally cheap at every step. In this paper, we propose work-conserving speculation (WCS), a design that jointly allocates draft and verification budgets per request in LLM serving, and present ForeSpark as its prototype. ForeSpark realizes WCS with (i) a context-aware pre-draft estimator that predicts acceptance for every candidate length from the target model's context features, (ii) a lightweight joint draft-verify scheduler that selects both lengths through a global sort, and (iii) a post-draft budget distribution that spends verification on the most promising tokens. Implemented on vLLM, ForeSpark improves throughput by up to 1.77x over the state-of-the-art DSpark and by 2.49x over autoregressive decoding at a matched per-request generation rate, without changing the output distribution. It also tolerates higher load, sustaining up to 1.51x the request rate of DSpark under latency service level objectives (SLOs).

record.abstract: Marine surface vehicles (MSVs) have attracted considerable attention for their commercial, scientific, and military applications. Owing to their favorable performance-to-cost ratio, shipboard cameras are widely used to detect and recognize potentially hazardous situations across diverse operational scenarios. However, visual perception is inevitably degraded by restricted conditions, including irregular motion of the imaging platform, adverse weather, and long imaging distances. To improve situational awareness and navigation capabilities, complementary sensors, such as the automatic identification system (AIS), radar, and light detection and ranging (LiDAR), etc., have become essential shipboard equipment. Multi-sensor fusion can provide richer perceptual information and help ensure navigational safety of MSVs in restricted visibility. This article reviews recent progress from intelligent vision to vision-centered multi-sensor fusion for newcomers and researchers in intelligent ship navigation and intelligent waterborne transportation system (IWTS). After introducing the generation of quality-degraded images in restricted visibility, we will review intelligent vision methods for four key issues, i.e., shipboard video stabilization, visual perception enhancement, object detection and tracking, and navigable area segmentation. We then examine vision-centered multi-sensor fusion methods, including infrared-visible image fusion, radar-vision fusion, LiDAR-vision fusion, AIS-vision fusion, and other multi-sensor fusion scenarios. Open-source datasets and safety-critical applications are also summarized and discussed. Finally, we highlight open challenges and future research directions. The collected maritime datasets are available at https://github.com/MAPGroup/Datasets and will be regularly updated.

record.abstract: Abstract The information we hold in mind with working memory (WM) may propagate beyond the cortex and out to the peripheral motor system. For instance, directionally biased hand and eye movements can express simple visuo-spatial features during WM maintenance. If such sensorimotor inflections are a form of WM representation, they may also express more multifaceted and task-adaptive information than just spatial location. Here, we ask whether gaze patterns carry item-specific detail about complex stimuli held in mind, and whether gaze prospectively adapts to the behavioral task demands. To do this, we tracked human eye movements (male and female) during WM for naturalistic images, and we manipulated which image features were most task-relevant (visual or semantic). In two experiments, we found that the eyes moved in complex, item-specific spatiotemporal sequences during WM maintenance. Delay period gaze patterns retraced the scanpaths from stimulus encoding, echoing the ‘gaze reinstatement’ that aligns with neural pattern reactivation during long-term memory retrieval. Therefore, gaze patterns during WM may reinstate visual encoding processes for maintenance. We also used time-resolved representational similarity analyses, guided by convolutional neural network modeling, to test the specificity of WM gaze patterns across a trial. We found that gaze representations were more distinct when the task prioritized visual detail, and also ramped up in anticipation of the WM probe. Therefore, oculomotor WM signals are malleable to when and how the content will be used. These results suggest that the earliest levels of visual processing reflect prospectively-oriented and functionally flexible WM content representations. Significance The eyes are an outwardly accessible extension of the brain. They are the first stop for visual processing, but may also offer a rich window into underlying cognition. For instance, pupil dilation can reflect changing cognitive load, and eye movement biases can reflect basic spatial information about content held in mind with working memory. Working memory is a critical neuro-cognitive function, but its physiological bases remain under debate. Here, we show that eye movements code for more than simple spatial WM, and instead express intricate patterns that read out the complex, real-world stimuli held in mind. This work shows how cognitive states influence oculomotor functions, and also advances theories of WM representation to include the earliest stages of sensory processing.

record.abstract: The discrepancy between early- and late-Universe determinations of the Hubble constant may point to physics beyond $Λ$CDM or to unaccounted-for systematics. Numerous late-time modifications to the expansion history have been proposed to alleviate this discrepancy, with limited success. Recent works have shown that, when the sound-horizon and supernova calibrations are held fixed, any purely late-time resolution requires a violation of the cosmic distance duality relation (CDDR). Recasting the tension in the $r_d$-$M_B$ plane, we show explicitly that distance duality, together with BAO and uncalibrated supernova data and a fixed sound-horizon calibration, determines $H_0$ independently of the late-time expansion history. We then test the viability of the required CDDR violation by separately constraining reciprocity violation and photon number non-conservation, deriving a new constraint on reciprocity-violating distortions of angular-diameter distances from BAO and cosmic-chronometer data. Combining this result with existing photon-number-conservation constraints, we find that the level of distance-duality violation needed to resolve the tension is strongly disfavoured by current data. We therefore conclude that, for fixed sound-horizon and supernova calibrations, no modification confined to the late-time expansion history -- even one violating distance duality -- can resolve the Hubble tension, pointing instead toward early-Universe physics or unresolved local systematics.

record.abstract: Dirichlet kernels provide a natural tool for density estimation on the simplex, but data-driven bandwidth selection for them has been mostly limited to likelihood cross-validation (LCV). We develop bandwidth selectors for Dirichlet kernel estimators of densities and projected first derivatives for compositional data. Using a Dirichlet mixture as the reference model, we derive an exact representation of the mean integrated squared error (MISE) and define the exact MISE (EMI) selector. We also derive a closed-form least-squares cross-validation (LSCV) criterion and introduce the reference-smoothed least-squares (RSLS) selector, which replaces the unstable leave-one-out term of LSCV with the fitted Dirichlet mixture. For derivative estimation, we obtain projected derivatives of the Dirichlet density and their integrability conditions, extend the new bandwidth selectors, and carry out kernel mean shift clustering on the simplex. Simulations show that EMI is the most competitive selector for larger samples and Dirichlet-like targets, RSLS generally performs best for small samples and is more stable than LSCV for derivative estimation, and LCV remains competitive for non-Dirichlet targets in density estimation. record.abstract: Existing generative model-based approaches to linear inverse problems typically use the acquired noisy measurement to condition or guide sampling in the image domain. In this work, we introduce Dual Flow, a novel joint flow model for solving linear inverse problems by jointly estimating the clean image and its corresponding noise-free measurement from the observation. Specifically, Dual Flow formulates image reconstruction and measurement denoising as a coupled estimation problem, using coupled flows in the image and measurement domains. The acquired noisy measurement $\mathbf{y}_0$ is used only to initialize the measurement state; thereafter, the image and measurement states are jointly updated based on their current values. By construction, the final image and measurement estimates are guaranteed to satisfy the underlying forward model. We derive the sampling updates for the joint flow and show that they are governed by the conditional mean of the clean image given the current joint state. We further derive a closed-form expression for a sufficient statistic of the joint state and show that the required conditional mean can be obtained by solving an image-domain Gaussian denoising problem involving operator-dependent, correlated noise. We train a velocity-prediction network using this formulation to estimate the conditional mean from the derived sufficient statistic. Dual Flow requires no hyperparameter tuning beyond selecting the number of inference steps and achieves substantially shorter reconstruction times than competing methods. Extensive experiments across various linear inverse problems and image datasets demonstrate state-of-the-art performance in both distortion metrics and perceptual quality. Additional analyses assess robustness to model mismatch, as well as the ability to generate diverse plausible reconstructions and characterize reconstruction uncertainty.

record.abstract: Innovative intersection designs can improve roadway safety and operational efficiency, but their uncommon geometries may create challenges for driver comprehension during early deployment. Evaluating these designs through full-scale field implementation can also be costly. This paper presents InterSim, a Unity game engine-based human-in-the-loop (HITL) driving simulator that constructs digital twins of site-specific innovative intersections in a virtual environment. InterSim links the real world and the simulation world through two closed cycles: a digital twin cycle that builds each intersection twin from agency design and traffic data and returns evidence from simulation to the agency, and an HITL cycle in which human drivers or automated driving algorithms operate the ego vehicle under identical scenario conditions. The research capabilities of InterSim are demonstrated through two case studies: a surrogate safety study compares post-encroachment time distributions between a Reduced Conflict Intersection and a standard intersection under different traffic volumes; an eco-driving study compares human drivers with a rule-based agent using vehicle-to-infrastructure information and reveals differences in emission and driving behavior. These studies demonstrate that InterSim provides a reusable digital twin platform for investigating innovative intersection designs from diverse perspectives. record.abstract: The rapid growth of electric vehicle (EV) adoption in Thailand has increased demand for charging infrastructure, particularly at high-density residential buildings with parking and electrical-capacity constraints. This study evaluates the techno-economic feasibility of installing two 60 kW DC chargers and two 22 kW AC chargers at a condominium in Bangkok, with an initial investment of THB 1,990,500 excluding VAT. The assessment integrates project quotations, site-specific electrical designs, charger specifications, and scenario-based financial modeling. Technical feasibility was assessed based on installation requirements, electrical compatibility, and safety provisions, while economic feasibility was evaluated using net present value (NPV), internal rate of return (IRR), and simple payback period (PB). The proposed configuration satisfied the specified technical requirements. Three utilization scenarios considered DC charging for 4–6 h/day and AC charging for 10–14 h/day. Electricity costs were modeled at THB 4.50/kWh, with additional increases of 2.5% and 5% and corresponding adjustments to charging prices. A 10-year project lifetime and a 5.5% discount rate were assumed. The results showed NPVs ranging from THB 382,947.62 to THB 3,527,186.83, IRRs from 9.34% to 34.94%, and PBs from 2.72 to 6.32 years. The best-performing scenario, with DC and AC utilization of 6 and 14 h/day, respectively, achieved an NPV of THB 3,527,186.83, an IRR of 34.94%, and a PB of 2.72 years. Charger utilization, particularly DC utilization, was a key determinant of economic viability. Mixed AC/DC charging infrastructure may therefore be economically attractive under the modeled conditions, although the utilization assumptions were not validated using long-term measured charging-demand data.

record.abstract: Promptable perception, from GroundingDINO to Rex-Omni, puts one model behind one prompt interface and returns coordinates for any localisation task. Every model in that line was built for photographs; none has been given a sketch. We present Sketch-Omni, to our knowledge the first perception MLLM built to work on sketches and from them. On a sketch, the sketch is the image, and text prompts detect, point, resolve object and spatial referring expressions, and ground affordances in it. From a sketch, the sketch is the prompt, and a drawing of one object localises that object in a photograph, even among several of the same category, a query that neither a category name nor a photo exemplar can pose. Two obstacles stand in the way. A photo-trained model's attention is tuned to colour and texture, which a sketch does not have, and no dataset pairs a drawing with the one instance it depicts among others of its kind. We build the training data instead of collecting it. An edge detector turns every labelled photograph into a sketch-like drawing that keeps the photograph's labels, and two constructions produce sketch-to-photo instance pairs from existing data. On top of this, photo-guided relation alignment passes each photograph and its edge sketch through the same model and trains the sketch pass to reproduce how the photograph pass relates phrases to patches and patches to each other. Not one training label is drawn by hand. Sketch-Omni reaches 91.4 F1 on sketch-prompted localisation against 81.8 for the strongest general-purpose MLLM, with a lead that doubles when the photograph holds several instances of the queried category, and it is best in 39 of 40 evaluation cells across six tasks. Code, model, and a hand-annotated benchmark of 2754 sketch-to-photo links will be released.

record.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Inherited ataxias are clinically diverse neurodegenerative diseases, complicating the choice of outcome measures for trials. We investigated whether the Upright Stability Score (USS), validated in Friedreich ataxia (FRDA), retains its psychometric properties in SCA, and how it compares with SARA, f-SARA, and the Friedreich Ataxia Activities of Daily Living scale (FA-ADL). METHODS: Cross-sectional data from ambulatory participants in two large international natural-history studies (CRC-SCA and UNIFAI) were analyzed with correlation-based psychometric methods, comparing score distributions across scales and genotypes. RESULTS: Data from 406/343 participants in CRC-SCA/UNIFAI were analyzed. In SCA, the USS captured a wider spectrum of balance performance, while in FRDA, early proprioceptive deficits-particularly impaired stance with eyes closed-constrained score variability. USS correlated strongly with SARA, f-SARA, and FA-ADL in both cohorts. SARA showed moderate skew, and f-SARA showed pronounced floor effects in mildly affected SCA, whereas USS and FA-ADL preserved discrimination at the low end. FA-ADL distributions were broadly comparable across genotypes. Limitations include cross-sectional design and a substantial age difference between cohorts.

record.abstract: Determining centrality of heavy-ion collisions with high resolution is essential for event-by-event analyses, in particular for net-proton fluctuation measurements aimed at locating the QCD critical point. Supervised machine-learning approaches rely on labels generated by model and therefore inherit the model dependence of the training target. In this work, we propose an unsupervised method to determine collision centrality based on optimal transport. Each collision is represented by its 1-Wasserstein distances to a fixed set of landmark events chosen to cover the measured multiplicity range. A point-cloud network trained by contrastive learning then compresses these distances into a compact event embedding, which is partitioned into equal-size centrality classes. We find that this approach groups events with similar $N_{\rm part}$ and yields a better centrality resolution, quantified by the normalized width of the $N_{\rm part}$ distribution, than the conventional method of cutting on particle multiplicity. The method, however, encounters a bottleneck once realistic kinematic cuts are applied to the particles. We attribute this degraded performance to the loss of distinct features between central and peripheral collisions because of applying kinematic cuts. The application of optimal transport to centrality determination in experimental data, remains an open problem that needs further study.

record.abstract: Continual model updating has become a common practice in the deployment of machine learning systems. However, the dynamic training behaviors give rise to new risks not sufficiently addressed by existing studies. In this paper, we present the first systematic study of temporal privacy risk in continually updated deep learning models. We formalize the notion of temporal membership in continually updated models. We then define the temporal membership inference attack, which seeks to infer whether and when individual samples were involved in model training, at both timestamp-level and interval-level granularities. To this end, we propose TMIA, a novel black-box attack that leverages bidirectional LSTMs to infer temporal membership from model outputs observed across successive updates. Through extensive experiments on three language models and three image classification models, we show that TMIA is highly effective and significantly outperforms existing baselines. Finally, we evaluate three potential defenses, revealing the trade-off between privacy protection and model utility.

record.abstract: Abstract We present measurements of the mass–metallicity relation (MZR) and fundamental metallicity relation (FMR) at 1.4 < z < 7.0 using stacked JWST/NIRSpec spectra of 601 star-forming galaxies from the JWST Advanced Deep Extragalactic Survey (JADES). Using the most up-to-date strong-line metallicity calibrations based on high-redshift galaxies, we derive gas-phase metallicities from composite spectra binned by stellar mass, redshift, and star-forming main sequence (SFMS) offset. We find that the MZR slope evolves weakly from z ∼ 0 out to ∼5, with γ ∼ 0.21 ± 0.03, while the normalization decreases smoothly with redshift at a rate of d log ( O / H ) / d z ∼ − 0.1 out to z ∼ 4. Beyond z ≳ 5, the low-mass end continues to decline in metallicity while the high-mass end remains broadly consistent with lower-redshift relations, producing a steeper overall MZR. We additionally find evidence for a shallow anticorrelation between deviations from the MZR and SFMS at fixed stellar mass at z ∼ 1.4−5. This anticorrelation, albeit with weaker star formation rate coupling than observed locally, suggests that an FMR is already beginning to emerge by z ∼ 5. Comparisons with recent observations and cosmological simulations show broad agreement, though no single simulation simultaneously reproduces the observed slopes and normalizations across all redshifts. Our results support a picture in which bursty star formation and strong stellar feedback increasingly shape the regulation of galaxy growth at high redshift, while also highlighting the need for substantially larger spectroscopic samples to robustly constrain the evolution of galaxy scaling relations at high redshift.

record.abstract: Accurate forecasting of renewable generation requires not only point predictions but also reliable estimates of the uncertainty attached to them, particularly at extended horizons. Machine learning models are increasingly used to predict solar output, but they typically report a single value and capture the associated uncertainty poorly. The standard remedy is to train a model to predict the parameters of an assumed probability distribution directly. Here we develop an alternative two-stage method, motivated by synthetic solar signal generation, in which the forecast error is modeled separately from the expected irradiance. A first long short-term memory (LSTM) network predicts the expected global horizontal irradiance, and a second network models the distribution of the forecast error, which is added back to the mean to give both the forecast and its uncertainty. Using historical weather data from the National Solar Radiation Database and a probability integral transform evaluation, we show that explicitly modeling the error brings the predicted standard deviation markedly closer to the historical value, reducing the deviation between the two by 34.6 percent for a standalone LSTM and by 56.5 percent when the LSTM is coupled to Gaussian process regression, the most reliable of the configurations tested. Because the method models the total forecast error directly, it captures the full predictive uncertainty that matters for decisions, rather than only the model contribution that dropout-based approaches estimate.

record.abstract: Quantum identity authentication is an effective solution for establishing mutual trust between communicating parties in the post-quantum era. The protocol first proposes a method of encoding a random sequence onto the probability amplitudes of quantum entangled states, forming perturbed probability amplitudes, thereby reducing the involvement of shared information between the sender and receiver. record.abstract: Causal set theory permits changes of spatial topology without the metric degeneracy that forbids them in continuum Lorentzian gravity. In four dimensions such changes enter the gravitational action only through the Gauss--Bonnet term, which is the Euler density. We show that the Euler density of a discrete space is exact, local and combinatorial: it sums to the Euler characteristic at any resolution and is supported on topological defects. The Gauss--Bonnet term of a causal set is therefore fixed rather than postulated. Because it is linear in the number of elements, which is the four-volume, it acts as a cosmological constant. Its coefficient follows without forming any functional derivative, so the known obstruction in the continuum does not arise. The everpresent cosmological constant of causal set theory assumes that the mean topological charge vanishes. We show that it does not. The species of opposite sign solves the field equations only if a positive cosmological constant is already present, and, being simply connected, it cannot carry the axion charge that supports the other species. Only one sign survives, and the sign of the cosmological term is derived rather than assumed. We recover the surviving transition from the causal order alone in every simulated sprinkling. The action of the corresponding axion wormhole then fixes the magnitude. The observed value requires an axion decay constant near the grand unification scale, and this result is insensitive to the one-loop prefactor and to the Gauss--Bonnet coupling.

record.abstract: Causal questions often arise in systems that evolve in continuous time. In this work, we develop an IV framework for stationary continuous-time stochastic processes parameterized by stochastic differential equations (SDE), where the instrument itself takes the form of a stochastic process. We encode the structural sparsity and causal effects directly at the infinitesimal level of the drift, and contrast these assumptions with the IV assumptions on the discretized version of the same process. Based on these structural assumptions, we derive moment restrictions using path-valued instruments. We show how these restrictions simplify for Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes and present an identification condition together with a corresponding consistent estimation method. Finally, we extend our estimation framework to nonlinear causal effects by expressing the path-based moment restrictions leveraging the signature kernel. Empirically, our method recovers causal effects in confounded continuous-time systems where maximum-likelihood-based estimation and discrete-time IV methods are systematically biased.

record.abstract: A bstract Employing the Schwinger-Keldysh formalism, we formulate an effective field theory for s-wave superconducting phase transition, where the dynamical variables consist of electromagnetic gauge field and complex scalar order parameter. Symmetry-constrained effective action allows systematic handling of dissipations and fluctuations. In particular, we explore the physical implications of higher-order terms, including those involving additional dynamical fields as well as higher time derivatives, on the real-time dynamics near the superconducting critical point. When appropriately truncated, the effective field theory reproduces the phenomenological Ginzburg-Landau equations. Upon crossing the critical temperature into the low-temperature phase, the electromagnetic gauge symmetry undergoes spontaneous breaking induced by the condensate of the order parameter. Collective excitation analysis reveals that the Higgs mode behaves as an overdamped diffusive mode near the critical point, while the phase fluctuation is absorbed into the gauge field via the Higgs mechanism. For complex kinetic coefficients, we derive the coupled linearized equations for amplitude, phase, and longitudinal gauge fluctuations, and distinguish propagation from damping through their complex poles. The holographic Schwinger-Keldysh construction provides an explicit realization and a nontrivial consistency check of the effective action, and determines its Wilsonian coefficients within a specific strongly coupled model. Holographic results reveal a complex relaxation parameter that indicates oscillatory dynamics characteristic of strongly coupled systems.

record.abstract: Universal Health Coverage (UHC) is central to Sustainable Development Goal 3.8, aiming to ensure equitable access to quality health services without financial hardship. East African countries, including Tanzania, Kenya, Uganda, and Rwanda, have demonstrated strong political commitment through policies, strategic plans, and national health insurance reforms. Despite these efforts, a significant gap persists between political declarations and practical implementation. Systemic barriers, such as limited financing, workforce shortages, governance weaknesses, affordability constraints, service delivery inefficiencies, and political instability, continue to impede progress. This article examines the commitment–practice gap, highlights underlying structural and operational challenges, and proposes policy strategies to accelerate UHC in the region. Key recommendations include strengthening domestic resource mobilisation, reinforcing primary health care, enhancing governance and accountability, and leveraging digital health innovations such as electronic health records, mobile insurance platforms, and telemedicine. It also emphasises well-structured public–private partnerships in service delivery, diagnostics, and supply chains, alongside the promotion of regional learning and cooperation through the East African Community (EAC). By translating political commitments into effective health system interventions, East African countries can move closer to achieving health equity and ensuring that health becomes a right rather than a privilege for all citizens.

record.abstract: Environment division multiple access (EDMA) has recently emerged as a promising multiple-access paradigm by exploiting the wireless propagation environment for user separation, while physical-layer security, including secrecy and covert communication, is becoming increasingly important for protecting confidential information and user privacy. Motivated by these considerations, this paper proposes an EDMA-enabled non-orthogonal multiple access for secrecy and covert communications (EDMA-NOMA-SC) framework for uplink wireless systems. In the proposed framework, a segmented-waveguide-enabled pinching antenna system (SWAN) is employed, where a secrecy user and an intermittently active covert user share the same transmission resource through NOMA within each segment, while a malicious warden attempts to eavesdrop on the secrecy transmission and detect the presence of the covert communication. To capture practical operating conditions, distance-dependent blockage, inter-segment interference, in-waveguide attenuation, imperfect channel state information (ipCSI), and imperfect successive interference cancellation (ipSIC) are considered. Semi-analytical frameworks are developed to characterize the secrecy outage probability (SOP), average secrecy capacity (ASC), false alarm probability (FAP), missed detection probability (MDP), detection error probability (DEP), and covert rate (CR), with their accuracy verified through Monte Carlo simulations. Numerical results, including comparisons with conventional and EDMA-based benchmark schemes, show that the proposed framework generally achieves improved secrecy and covert-rate performance owing to reduced user-to-pinching-antenna propagation distances and in-waveguide attenuation. record.abstract: In integrated sensing and communication (ISAC), the same base-station array beamforms toward users and estimates their angle of arrival (AoA). In this paper, we study how element-level gain, phase, and position errors affect both functions of a beam-scanning uniform linear array. Any array produces a correlation peak at the true angle, of finite height and width, surrounded by sidelobes. Impairments shift this peak, make it lower and wider, and raise the sidelobes relative to it. A single decomposition explains these three effects: the gain-weighted least-squares fit of the per-antenna phase errors splits them into a tilt, which shifts the peak, and a residual, whose power is taken from the peak and redistributed over the sidelobes according to its spatial spectrum. A beam steered toward the strongest direction suffers from the lower peak only, whereas the AoA estimate suffers from its shift even without noise, and also from the lowering and sidelobes with noise. The worst cases for the two ISAC functions are thus nearly disjoint, and we characterize both: the worst case for beamforming leaves the AoA estimate unbiased, and the worst case for localization loses little beamforming gain. The worst case for localization is a single defect at the junction between two subarrays, and its error, relative to the main-lobe width, does not decrease with the number of antennas. We also characterize random impairments and the effect of noise. In practical terms, our analysis shows that the calibration of a dual-function array must be assessed with respect to both functions.

record.abstract: In networked integrated sensing and communication (ISAC), a base station (BS) performing sensing using its own downlink signals is subject to interference from the downlink transmissions of neighboring BSs. This paper investigates the impact of the signal constellation and waveform on the sensing performance in the presence of such inter-BS interference. For any linear receiver, we show that the mean-squared cross-ambiguity between two random ISAC signals is invariant to the modulation bases and constellations. We then derive the exact Fisher information under finite-alphabet interference with a flat-fading link, which equals the interference-free Fisher information scaled by $1-γ\,\mmse_{\C}(γ)$, where $γ$ denotes the interference-to-noise ratio (INR) and $\mmse_{\C}$ is the minimum mean-square error (MMSE) in estimating an interfering data symbol from its noise-corrupted observation at the sensing receiver. Consequently, Gaussian interference is the worst case and corresponds to the CRB loss of the matched filtering, whereas finite-alphabet interference induces a non-monotonic CRB loss that peaks at intermediate INR and vanishes at high INR. record.abstract: Accelerated particle beams are essential tools of modern science and technology with applications ranging from medicine [1], to light sources [2], to high-energy physics [3]. Over time, as accelerator-based experiments become more sophisticated and probe natural phenomena with greater temporal resolution, there is an increasing demand on beam parameters, in particular on bunch duration. Experiments have been proposed that require beams with 1-2 orders of magnitude shorter durations than what is possible with current state-of-the-art technology. However, state-of-the-art temporal bunch compressors force a trade-off between how short an electron bunch can be made and how well its transverse quality survives the strong bending magnets required to do so -- a limitation that stands as a grand challenge for accelerator physics to-date [4]. In this experiment, we demonstrate a new, compact compression technique for generating ultrashort, high-peak-current electron bunches that circumvents this trade-off using plasma wakefield acceleration. Just as chirped pulse amplification unlocked ultrashort, high-power laser pulses and the technologies that followed from them, here we demonstrate an analogous chirp-and-compress strategy applied to relativistic electron beams by using the extreme electric fields of a plasma wakefield in place of a stretcher-amplifier, thereby unlocking the path to ultrashort, extremely high-current electron beams. We demonstrate the first application of this plasma-compressed bunch using it to drive single-microbunch free electron lasing at optical wavelengths in a single, meter-scale undulator module, producing radiation pulses roughly four orders of magnitude more energetic than the first beam-driven, plasma-based free electron laser demonstration at the same accelerator facility [5, 6].

record.abstract: In natural human-AI dialogue, users' corrections, requests, and self-descriptions carry reusable signals about how they want work to be done. These signals reveal individual process preferences, user-specific standards for evidence, depth, analytical focus, procedure, and delivery. We ask whether a preference revealed in one dialogue can shape an assistant's later answer when the task does not restate it. ProcessPrefBench uses three months of natural dialogues from two knowledge workers to build 66 source-target cases separately judged for source evidence and target applicability. Sources are preselected, so the benchmark tests application rather than retrieval. We test three models with target-only, full-history, and distilled-preference prompts. Target-specific 0-2 rubrics score preference realization, and a task gate flags severe failures. Compared with target-only prompting, full-history and imperative distilled-preference prompting raise preference realization by 0.204 and 0.244 points on the 0-2 scale, respectively, with no reliable advantage from distillation. Fabricated-evidence failures rise from 5.8% under target-only prompting to 10.1% under full-history and 10.4% under imperative prompting. ProcessPrefBench highlights a tension in learning from dialogue, where drawing on prior interactions can improve preference realization yet also invite fabricated evidence. We hope it helps build assistants that honor a user's process preferences without sacrificing factual reliability.

record.abstract: Background: Incomplete clinical records and imbalanced diagnostic groups complicate Parkinsonian classification. record.abstract: We investigate the role of quantum state texture in dynamical quantum phase transitions by establishing a direct connection between critical nonequilibrium dynamics and the recently introduced notion of rugosity, a measure of quantum state texture. Considering a generic quench protocol, we analyze both standard formulations of dynamical quantum phase transitions. For type-I transitions, characterized through the long-time behavior of a dynamical order parameter, we show that the time-averaged rugosity, evaluated in the eigenbasis of the pre-quench Hamiltonian, exhibits an order-parameter-like behavior across the transition. In the Lipkin-Meshkov-Glick model, this behavior is traced back to the underlying semiclassical structure, where crossing the excited-state quantum phase transition separatrix controls the redistribution of the quantum state over the pre-quench energy basis. We further demonstrate that the response function associated with the time-averaged rugosity develops a pronounced critical peak whose maximum grows algebraically with the system size, providing quantitative finite-size evidence of its sensitivity to the dynamical critical point. For type-II transitions, characterized by nonanalyticities in the Loschmidt rate function, we establish an exact connection with rugosity. For a suitable choice of basis, the rate function is exactly given by the density of rugosity, establishing a model-independent equivalence. Moreover, we show that even in physically motivated bases, such as the pre-quench energy eigenbasis, rugosity provides clear signatures of dynamical criticality. Our results establish rugosity as a sensitive probe of dynamical quantum phase transitions while highlighting its role as a basis-dependent measure of quantum state texture, thereby providing an information-theoretic perspective on nonequilibrium quantum critical phenomena.

record.abstract: ABSTRACT The plasmonic lightning‐rod effect refers to the formation of a strong electric near field of localized surface plasmons at the sharp features of plasmonic antennas. Although this effect is intuitively utilized in the design and optimization of plasmonic antennas, the relation between the magnitude of the electric field and the local curvature of the plasmonic antenna has not yet been rigorously established. Here, we provide such a study. We design sets of plasmonic antennas that allow us to isolate the role of the local curvature from other effects influencing the field. The electric near field is inspected by electron energy‐loss spectroscopy and electrodynamic simulations. We confirm the existence of the plasmonic lightning‐rod effect, demonstrate its decoupling from concurrent effects influencing the field, and establish its quantitative description, showing that its strength can be interpreted as comparable to that of the electrostatic lightning‐rod effect. We also provide a simple empirical formula for the spatial dependence of the field, which includes the effective radius of curvature significantly smaller than the geometrical radius.

record.abstract: The L-arginine is essential amino acid for birds because they have limited ability to produce enough endogenous L-arginine. In addition to its role in protein synthesis, arginine serves as a precursor of polyamines, creatine, proline, other bioactive metabolites, and nitric oxide, which are involved in growth, immune function, antioxidant defense, integrity of the intestine, reproduction, and cell signaling. The purpose of this review was to critically appraise the present understanding on the metabolism, physiological role and application of l-arginine supplementation to the nutrition of various types of poultry especially broiler chickens, laying hens, breeder flocks and Japanese quail. Therefore, experimental studies have shown that providing sufficient levels of arginine in the diet is crucial for optimum growth performance, feed efficiency, skeletal muscle development, reproductive performance and immune competence. These beneficial effects are most clearly demonstrated when nutrients are added at times of high growth rate, heat stress, oxidative stress, immune challenge, or when dietary arginine is low. However, excessive supplementation beyond the physiological requirement does not always result in an increase in productive performance and can influence the amino acid balance, especially when the level is increased with lysine. Recent studies in molecular biology have shown that arginine affects several signaling pathways such as nitric oxide synthase, mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR), phosphoinositide 3-kinase/protein kinase B (PI3K/Akt), and polyamine biosynthesis, which in turn impact nutrient utilization, intestinal development, cellular proliferation, and stress adaptation. Further, emerging evidence indicates that arginine regulates gut microbiota and gut host–microbe interaction, which opens the possibilities for gut health and disease resistance. However, this is achieved while there is great variation within published studies ranging from species of birds, genotype, age, diet, environmental factors and experimental design. Future studies should combine transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics and microbiome studies with standardized dose-response studies to clarify precise nutritional recommendations for various poultry production systems. In conclusion, L-arginine is not just an amino acid that is essential to poultry but a multifunctional nutritional regulator that has considerable potential to enhance poultry health, welfare and productivity when fed at the correct dietary level.

record.abstract: High-quality material generation for physically based rendering (PBR) remains challenging because datasets and synthesis pipelines lack standardized representations. Differences in material definitions, rendering conventions, and parameterizations lead to unstable and physically implausible results. We propose MIKU, a unified framework for standardized PBR asset representation and physically consistent material generation across diverse 3D content domains. Its core is a unified processing pipeline that standardizes the workflow from data preprocessing to final texture synthesis, maintaining consistent geometry and texture representations. A normalization scheme harmonizes heterogeneous material parameterizations in a common representation space, enabling robust cross-dataset training and inference. Building on this formulation, we train a novel physically aware diffusion model for PBR texture generation within a two-stage multi-view synthesis framework. First, geometry-aware albedo generation synthesizes multi-view albedo maps under explicit geometric guidance to ensure cross-view appearance consistency. Second, metallic-roughness generation uses the diffusion model to predict physically plausible roughness and metallic maps conditioned on the generated albedo and unified representation. Trained end-to-end on standardized data, the model learns to generate materials that respect category-level material priors and semantic part boundaries. By decoupling representation standardization from appearance synthesis, MIKU substantially improves material generation stability and physical consistency. Extensive experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art texture quality and semantic consistency across object parts, advancing automated material generation for 3D content creation.

record.abstract: In the Telephone Broadcast problem we are given a graph G = ( V , E ) with a designated source vertex s ∈ V . Our goal is to transmit a message, which is initially known only to s , to all vertices of the graph by using a process where in each round an informed vertex may transmit the message to one of its uninformed neighbors. The optimization objective is to minimize the number of rounds. Following up on several recent works, we investigate the structurally parameterized complexity of Telephone Broadcast . In particular, we first strengthen existing NP-hardness results by showing that the problem remains NP-complete on graphs of bounded tree-depth and also on cactus graphs which are one vertex deletion away from being path forests. Motivated by this (severe) hardness, we study several other parameterizations of the problem and obtain FPT algorithms parameterized by vertex integrity (generalizing a recent FPT algorithm parameterized by vertex cover by Fomin, Fraigniaud, and Golovach [TCS 2024]) and by distance to clique, as well as FPT approximation algorithms parameterized by clique-cover and cluster vertex deletion. Furthermore, we obtain structural results that relate the length of the optimal broadcast protocol of a graph G with its pathwidth and tree-depth. By presenting a substantial improvement over the best previously known bound for pathwidth (Aminian, Kamali, Seyed-Javadi, and Sumedha [ICALP 2025]) we exponentially improve the approximation ratio achievable in polynomial time on graphs of bounded pathwidth from \(\mathcal {O}(4^\mathrm{pw}) \) to \(\mathcal {O}(\mathrm{pw}) \) .

record.abstract: Semantic information can enrich the identifiers and structured fields used by recommender systems. Semantic tokenization provides a structured representation of this information by converting LLM-derived user profiles into discrete tokens. In the common two-stage pipeline, the tokenizer is trained before the recommender. Its token assignments are then treated as fixed input features during recommendation training. As a result, the downstream recommender can learn how to use the assigned indices, but it cannot revise the semantic partition that produced them. Making this partition task-aware is difficult because nearest-code assignment is discrete, and unconstrained adaptation may also distort the geometry learned during pretraining. Moreover, a fixed token depth exposes the same semantic resolution to every interaction. We thus propose OptST (Optimizing Semantic Tokenization), which makes a pretrained tokenizer responsive to downstream recommendation. To revise token assignments without directly updating the pretrained encoder or base codebooks, OptST learns a low-rank deformation whose drift is limited by an anchor regularizer. Recommendation supervision reaches this transformation through a straight-through estimator, while prediction retains hard nearest-code assignments. Beyond adapting the assignments themselves, OptST selects an interaction-conditioned prefix to control how much residual detail is exposed to the recommender. Experiments on four public datasets show that OptST achieves the highest AUC among conventional and LLM-enhanced baselines. Its improvements also persist across different recommendation backbones. These results establish task-aware semantic tokenization as an effective interface between LLM-derived profiles and downstream recommendation models.

record.abstract: As large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to simulate human behavior, their operational validity is typically assessed through accuracy alone, implicitly treating human behavior as deterministic. We argue that on noisy digital trace data, a model's performance depends not only on predicting the correct outcome but on its calibration. record.abstract: In mission-critical networks, a missed jamming event is costlier than a false alarm, so detectors should favor recall, operate causally, and work without labeled attack data. record.abstract: Predicting stock returns requires modeling persistent company relations and time-varying market signals. Graph Neural Network (GNN) approaches combine static priors with dynamic relational graphs, but treat every extracted edge as a trustworthy binary fact, ignoring heterogeneous reliability across relational sources. A context-dependent gated fusion module rebalances the two graphs at the per-stock, per-day level. record.abstract: Planning has been identified as an important factor for improved code generation with Large Language Models (LLMs). However, the interaction between planning capability and coding capability remains largely underexplored, especially when the two capabilities are from different LLMs. In this paper, we conduct the first comprehensive empirical study of planning-coding interaction in LLM-based code generation, where planning and coding are assigned to different LLMs (i.e., planning-coding separation). Specifically, we explore different planner-coder combinations to investigate the effectiveness for coders to utilize planning information from various planners and the impact of further training of coders on planner-coder combinations. Our results demonstrate that almost all planner-coder combinations are as competitive as using the same LLM for planning and coding, and the combination of a stronger planner and a stronger coder typically achieves improved effectiveness. These findings provide empirical evidence that planning and coding can be separated to a considerable extent in LLM-based code generation, which may offer a more flexible way to construct code-generation systems.
